name: Faster Payment Initiation
orchestration_notes: Channel makes a single synchronous call to SVC-001 (POST /payments) to create a PaymentIntent. All subsequent cross-capability coordination is event-driven via SVC-102 (event bus). The channel polls GET /payments/{id} for status updates. No capability ever calls another capability's API directly.
sca_method: FIDO2/WebAuthn biometric or TOTP — FCA SCA (PSD2/PSRs 2017 Article 4). Dynamic linking required: SCA must bind to payee account number, sort code, and amount.

phases.name: Payment Initiation
phases.description: Customer accesses the payments section of the web or mobile channel, selects or adds a payee, enters payment amount and reference, and triggers Confirmation of Payee (CoP) check. The customer then completes Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) via FIDO2/WebAuthn biometric or TOTP. On successful SCA, the channel calls SVC-001 POST /payments to create a PaymentIntent with status = pending_screening.
persona_actions: Select 'Make a Payment' in the channel UI
Choose existing payee or add new payee (sort code + account number + name)
Enter amount (GBP, max 2 decimal places) and optional payment reference (max 18 chars, Faster Payments reference field)
Review CoP result — match, partial match, or no match
If no-match or partial-match: read fraud risk warning and actively confirm intent to proceed
Complete SCA (biometric or TOTP) — dynamic linking to payee sort code, account number, and amount
system_actions: Channel calls CoP service (external, via SVC-009) to verify payee name against receiving bank record
Channel renders CoP result with PSR SD17-compliant risk warnings for no-match and partial-match
Customer completes SCA (FIDO2 biometric or TOTP); SVC-100 validates assertion
Channel calls SVC-001 POST /payments — creates PaymentIntent with status = pending_screening
SVC-001 validates account status (active), available balance >= amount, daily payment limit not exceeded
SVC-001 publishes PaymentIntentCreated event (EVT-P01)
phases.exit_condition: PaymentIntent created with status = pending_screening; EVT-P01 published
nfr_references: SCA completion < 30 seconds customer action budget

phases.name: Pre-Execution Checks
phases.description: Asynchronous compliance and fraud checks run concurrently after PaymentIntentCreated. SVC-051 (Sanctions Screening) and SVC-013 (Fraud Detection) both consume PaymentIntentCreated and run their checks independently. SVC-001 waits for both SanctionsScreeningCompleted (EVT-P02) and FraudScoreCompleted (EVT-P03) before proceeding.
channel: No customer-facing interaction during this phase — customer sees a 'processing' state
persona_actions: Customer waits on confirmation screen; channel shows animated progress indicator
No customer action required unless a CoP override confirmation was deferred
system_actions: SVC-051 consumes PaymentIntentCreated: runs real-time OFSI/UN/EU/US OFAC sanctions screen against payee sort code + account number + beneficiary name. Publishes SanctionsScreeningCompleted (EVT-P02)

SVC-013 consumes PaymentIntentCreated: runs ML fraud scoring against payment amount, payee, channel, device fingerprint, behavioural biometrics, and account history. Publishes FraudScoreCompleted (EVT-P03)
SVC-001 waits for both EVT-P02 and EVT-P03. On receipt of both with outcome = clear, SVC-001 publishes PaymentCleared (EVT-P04)
If either check returns a hit or block, SVC-001 publishes PaymentFailed (EVT-P07) or PaymentFraudBlocked (EVT-P08) as appropriate
phases.exit_condition: Both SanctionsScreeningCompleted and FraudScoreCompleted received. Outcome is either clear (→ PY-003) or blocked (→ exception path)

phases.name: Payment Decision
phases.description: SVC-001 evaluates the combined outcomes of sanctions and fraud checks. If both clear, SVC-001 publishes PaymentCleared (EVT-P04). If a fraud block is triggered, SVC-001 publishes PaymentFraudBlocked (EVT-P08) and the channel informs the customer the payment cannot proceed. If a sanctions hit is detected, SVC-001 publishes PaymentFailed (EVT-P07) with a generic decline reason (tipping-off prohibition applies — specific sanctions match must not be disclosed to customer).
persona_actions: If approved: customer continues to see processing confirmation screen
If fraud blocked: customer sees generic 'We were unable to process your payment' message with contact details
If sanctions hit: customer sees generic decline message — no disclosure of sanctions match (MLR 2017 tipping-off prohibition)
system_actions: SVC-001 evaluates EVT-P02 and EVT-P03 outcomes
All clear → SVC-001 publishes PaymentCleared (EVT-P04)
Fraud score above threshold → SVC-001 publishes PaymentFraudBlocked (EVT-P08); PER-054 (Fraud Analyst) notified for investigation
Sanctions hit → MLRO (PER-052) notified; SVC-001 publishes PaymentFailed (EVT-P07) with reason = sanctions_review
Insufficient funds (validated at PY-001 but re-checked for race condition) → SVC-001 publishes PaymentFailed (EVT-P07) with reason = insufficient_funds
phases.exit_condition: Payment is either cleared (→ PY-004) or terminal failure event published and customer notified

phases.name: FPS Execution
phases.description: SVC-009 (Domestic Payments) consumes PaymentCleared (EVT-P04) and submits the payment to the Faster Payments Service via Pay.UK/Vocalink infrastructure. On successful scheme acceptance, SVC-009 publishes PaymentExecuted (EVT-P05) with the FPS end-to-end transaction reference. SVC-001 consumes PaymentExecuted, debits the account ledger, and publishes AccountDebited (EVT-P06).
channel: No customer-facing interaction — customer sees pending confirmation screen
persona_actions: Customer polling GET /payments/{id} sees status = processing → executed
system_actions: SVC-009 consumes PaymentCleared (EVT-P04)
SVC-009 formats and submits FPS instruction to Pay.UK/Vocalink (ISO 20022 pacs.008 message)
Vocalink processes and routes payment to receiving bank
SVC-009 receives FPS acceptance and scheme reference; publishes PaymentExecuted (EVT-P05) with fps_reference, execution_timestamp, settlement_status = accepted
SVC-001 consumes PaymentExecuted (EVT-P05); debits account ledger by payment amount; updates PaymentIntent.status = completed
SVC-001 publishes AccountDebited (EVT-P06)
SVC-051 consumes PaymentExecuted for audit log (OFSI compliance — all screening decisions and outcomes must be logged)
phases.exit_condition: PaymentExecuted and AccountDebited events published; PaymentIntent.status = completed

phases.name: Confirmation
phases.description: Channel detects payment completion via polling GET /payments/{id} — status = completed. The channel renders the payment confirmation screen to the customer showing payee name, amount, FPS reference, estimated receipt time, and CoP result. SVC-053 dispatches a payment confirmation notification (push notification and/or email).
persona_actions: Customer notes FPS payment reference for their records
Customer may download or share confirmation
system_actions: Channel polls GET /payments/{id}; receives status = completed
Channel renders confirmation screen: payee name (CoP-verified), amount, currency, FPS reference, timestamp
SVC-053 dispatches payment confirmation notification (push notification to mobile, email confirmation to registered email address)
SVC-103 records completed payment in audit log
SVC-014 (KYC/AML) consumes AccountDebited for ongoing transaction monitoring (GOV-005-R01)
phases.exit_condition: Customer views confirmation screen; payment confirmation notification dispatched

happy_path.description: Customer initiates a Faster Payment, CoP returns a match, SCA completes, sanctions check is clear, fraud score is below threshold, payment executes via FPS successfully, account is debited, customer receives confirmation. Total elapsed time < 15 seconds from SCA completion to confirmation screen render.

alternative_paths.name: Scheduled Payment (Future-Dated)
alternative_paths.description: Customer selects a future payment date. PaymentIntent is created with status = scheduled and payment_date set to a future date. No immediate screening is triggered. On the payment_date, a scheduled job re-triggers the screening flow (PY-002 → PY-005). Customer can cancel at any time before processing begins.
additional_events: PaymentScheduled (variant of PaymentIntentCreated with future payment_date)

alternative_paths.name: Confirmation of Payee — Partial Match
alternative_paths.description: CoP returns a partial match (payee name similar but not exact). The channel displays a PSR SD17-compliant risk warning. Customer must actively confirm intent to proceed — passive timeout is not acceptable (GOV-003-R02). Customer proceeds → payment creation flow continues from SCA step.
alternative_paths.customer_action_required: Explicit confirmation click — cannot be a timeout or passive action

alternative_paths.name: Confirmation of Payee — No Match
alternative_paths.description: CoP returns a no match. Channel displays prominent APP fraud risk warning. Customer must read and explicitly confirm to proceed. Channel records the customer override decision in the PaymentIntent audit trail (required for PSR APP fraud reimbursement gross negligence defence assessment).
alternative_paths.customer_action_required: Explicit 'I understand the risk and want to proceed' confirmation — with recorded timestamp
alternative_paths.app_fraud_reimbursement_note: CoP override is not automatic disqualification from APP fraud reimbursement. Gross negligence standard under PSR PS23/3 requires the customer to have explicitly been warned and to have acted unreasonably. Override is audit-recorded but does not automatically forfeit reimbursement entitlement.

exception_paths.name: Sanctions Hit Detected
exception_paths.description: SVC-051 returns a sanctions match on the payee. SVC-001 publishes PaymentFailed (EVT-P07) with reason = sanctions_review. MLRO (PER-052) is notified via SVC-103 alert. Customer sees a generic 'Payment cannot be processed' message — tipping-off prohibition (GOV-005-R02, POCA 2002 s333A) prohibits disclosing that a sanctions check is the reason. The PaymentIntent is retained in status = sanctions_blocked in the audit trail.
exception_paths.customer_message: Generic decline — 'We were unable to process this payment. Please contact us if you need further information.'
exception_paths.internal_action: MLRO alert raised; OFSI notification within 14 days if designated person confirmed

exception_paths.name: Fraud Block
exception_paths.description: SVC-013 fraud score exceeds the block threshold. SVC-001 publishes PaymentFraudBlocked (EVT-P08). Fraud Analyst (PER-054) is notified for investigation. Customer sees a generic decline message. The customer may be prompted to call the bank's fraud team to authenticate and manually override if the payment is genuine.
exception_paths.customer_message: 'We've blocked this payment for your security. Please call [fraud line] if you initiated this payment.'
exception_paths.internal_action: PER-054 (Fraud Analyst) case created; payment placed in fraud review queue

exception_paths.name: Insufficient Funds
exception_paths.description: Account available balance is insufficient to cover the payment amount. Detected at PaymentIntent creation (PY-001) — SVC-001 validates balance before publishing PaymentIntentCreated. If a race condition causes the balance check to fail post-creation, PaymentFailed is published with reason = insufficient_funds.
exception_paths.trigger: Available balance < payment amount at validation point
exception_paths.customer_message: 'Insufficient funds. Your available balance is [X]. Please reduce the payment amount or top up your account.'
exception_paths.internal_action: No internal alert required; customer is shown their available balance

exception_paths.name: FPS Timeout / Scheme Rejection
exception_paths.description: SVC-009 submits to FPS but receives a timeout (> 15 seconds) or a scheme-level rejection (e.g. invalid account at receiving bank, scheme downtime). SVC-009 publishes PaymentFailed (EVT-P07) with the FPS reject reason code. SVC-001 does not debit the account. Customer sees a payment failure message with advice to retry or contact support.
exception_paths.trigger: FPS submission timeout or pacs.002 rejection from Vocalink
exception_paths.customer_message: 'Your payment could not be completed. No money has left your account. Please try again or contact support.'
exception_paths.internal_action: Payment Operations on-call team alerted for scheme-level failures affecting multiple payments; individual timeouts handled by automatic retry logic in SVC-009 (max 2 retries with 3-second backoff)
exception_paths.retry_policy: SVC-009 retries FPS submission up to 2 times with exponential backoff before publishing PaymentFailed

exception_paths.name: Daily Payment Limit Exceeded
exception_paths.description: The payment amount would exceed the customer's configured daily payment limit (Account.daily_payment_limit). Detected at PaymentIntent creation. Customer is informed of their daily limit and the current day's total payment amount.
exception_paths.customer_message: 'This payment would exceed your daily payment limit of [X]. Your total payments today are [Y].'

design_decisions.decision: The channel makes a single synchronous API call (POST /payments to SVC-001) to initiate the payment. All pre-execution checks (sanctions, fraud) run asynchronously via events. The channel polls GET /payments/{id} for status.
design_decisions.rationale: This is the canonical event-driven pattern per the bank's architecture principle: 'The channel orchestrates the user interaction; the event bus orchestrates the cross-capability consequences.' A single API call keeps the channel simple and resilient. Polling is preferred over webhooks for the channel because the channel session has bounded duration and WebSocket complexity is not warranted for a < 15-second flow.

design_decisions.decision: Sanctions and fraud checks run concurrently after PaymentIntentCreated, not sequentially. Both publish independent events. SVC-001 waits for both before publishing PaymentCleared.
design_decisions.rationale: Sequential execution would add latency (3s sanctions + 0.5s fraud = 3.5s minimum). Concurrent execution means total wait is max(3s, 0.5s) ≈ 3 seconds. At FPS volumes (5B+ annual UK transactions) this latency reduction is material for customer experience and system throughput.

design_decisions.decision: CoP check is performed synchronously by the channel UI before the PaymentIntent is created (before POST /payments). It is not an async event.
design_decisions.rationale: CoP is a customer-interactive check — the result must be shown to the customer for them to confirm or abort. It cannot be async. The channel calls the CoP API (via SVC-009 which proxies to the Pay.UK CoP service) synchronously as part of the payment entry flow, before SCA.

design_decisions.decision: SCA dynamic linking (binding the authentication to the specific payee and amount) is enforced at the channel layer before the PaymentIntent is created.
design_decisions.rationale: PSRs 2017 Regulation 71 requires dynamic linking for push payments. The SCA must be completed before the payment instruction is submitted. This places the SCA obligation on the channel (SVC-017 / SVC-100), which is the appropriate owner.
